record.original_question: Consider a closed surface of genus ≥ 2 with a metric of non-positive curvature.

evidence.quote: Consider a closed surface of genus ≥ 2 with a metric of non-positive curvature.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M, g)$ be a smooth closed (compact, boundaryless) Riemannian surface of genus $\geq 2$ whose Gaussian curvature satisfies $K \leq 0$ everywhere. Let $SM$ denote the unit tangent bundle of $M$, equipped with its Liouville measure $\mu$ (the smooth probability measure induced by the Sasaki metric, or equivalently the Lebesgue measure on $SM$ associated with the metric $g$), and let $\varphi_t : SM \to SM$ be the geodesic flow.

It is known that $\varphi_t$ preserves $\mu$, and that the restriction of the flow to the (open, flow-invariant) set $\Sigma = \{ v \in SM : \text{the geodesic } \gamma_v \text{ passes through a point where } K < 0 \}$ is ergodic. The complementary set $SM \setminus \Sigma$ consists of unit vectors tangent to geodesics along which the curvature vanishes identically.

Question: Is the geodesic flow $\varphi_t$ on $SM$ ergodic with respect to the Liouville measure $\mu$? Equivalently, must the set $SM \setminus \Sigma$ of vectors tangent to "flat" (zero-curvature) geodesics have $\mu$-measure zero?
artifact.category_tag: Geodesic flows on nonpositively curved surfaces
artifact.status_search_result: Multiple recent sources (2015–2024) describe the ergodicity of the geodesic flow with respect to the Liouville measure on a closed surface of genus ≥ 2 with nonpositive curvature as a well-known open problem, with partial results (e.g. ergodicity assuming the set of negative-curvature points has finitely many connected components, by Burns–Gelfert and others). The general case remains unresolved, the obstruction being control of the measure of "flat" zero-curvature geodesics.

status_evidence.title: On the ergodicity of geodesic flows on surfaces of nonpositive curvature (Burns–Gelfert)
status_evidence.snippet: Ergodicity of the geodesic flow on a surface of genus ≥ 2 with nonpositive curvature is established under the assumption that the set of points of negative curvature has finitely many connected components; the general problem is described as open.
status_evidence.claim: Ergodicity of the geodesic flow with respect to Liouville measure on closed nonpositively curved surfaces of genus ≥ 2 is an open problem, with partial progress.

status_evidence.title: On ergodic properties of geodesic flows on uniform visibility manifolds without conjugate points (2024)
status_evidence.snippet: For surfaces of nonpositive curvature, the ergodicity of the geodesic flow with respect to the Liouville measure is widely open since the 1980's, due to the existence of flat geodesics.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is widely regarded as still open.

status_evidence.title: Open problems and questions about geodesics (Burns–Matveev)
status_evidence.snippet: Lists the ergodicity of the geodesic flow on closed nonpositively curved surfaces of higher genus as an open question.
status_evidence.claim: The problem appears in standard open-problem lists.
